body.name: Two-motif exact certificate
body.construction: For \(H=K_3\) and \(H=C_4\), build \(\mathfrak P_H\) from the lexicographic \(2^h\)-row assignment table. Since every vertex has degree two, row reduction of the three exposure moments gives \(w_a(0)=8\), \(w_a(1/2)=-8\), and \(w_a(1)=8\). Eliminate the \(3h\) bounded-schedule variables from \(q\ge F_H(w,b)\) using rational univariate representation. The \(K_3\) instance has eight assignment rows, nine weight coordinates, nine nuisance variables, and forty-eight assignment-indexed signed schedule inequalities; after removing duplicates, write \(p_i=y_i(0,0)\), \(q_i=y_i(1,0)\), \(r_i=y_i(0,1)\), and \(s_i=q_i+r_i-p_i=y_i(1,1)\), so its legal domain is the twelve polynomial inequalities \(1-p_i^2\ge0\), \(1-q_i^2\ge0\), \(1-r_i^2\ge0\), and \(1-s_i^2\ge0\) for \(i=1,2,3\). The exact upper certificate is the quantified implication that these twelve inequalities imply \(F_{K_3}(w,b)\le v_{K_3}\). The \(C_4\) instance has sixteen rows, twelve weight coordinates, twelve nuisance variables, and one hundred twenty-eight assignment-indexed signed schedule inequalities. For \(K_3\), let \(x_\triangle=(-13+2\sqrt{55})/17\), the unique root in \((0,1)\) of \(17x^2+26x-3=0\), and take the three vertex coefficient rows to be \((1,-(1+x_\triangle),-(1-x_\triangle))\), \((1,0,0)\), and \((-1,2,0)\). For assignments \(000,001,010,011,100,101,110,111\), the corresponding outcome rows are \((1,1,-1)\), \(((1+x_\triangle)/2,1,1)\), \(((1+x_\triangle)/2,1,-1)\), \((x_\triangle,1,1)\), \((-x_\triangle,1,-1)\), \((-(1+x_\triangle)/2,1,1)\), \((-(1+x_\triangle)/2,1,-1)\), and \((-1,1,1)\); hence every displayed outcome lies in \([-1,1]\). The resulting statistic rows are \(24\), four copies of \(-2x_\triangle^2-4x_\triangle-2\), two copies of \(8x_\triangle^2-16\), and \(24\), with mean \((1-x_\triangle)^2\) and variance \(17x_\triangle^4+12x_\triangle^3-58x_\triangle^2+12x_\triangle+209\). Quantifier elimination of the displayed implication certifies the matching upper bound; equivalently, \(v_{K_3}\) is the unique root in \((209,210)\) of \(4913v^2-1537792v+106463232=0\), and equality holds at this legal schedule. For \(C_4\), the legal constant schedule \(y_{b,a}(z)=1\) has statistic rows \(32,0,0,-32,0,32,-32,0,0,-32,32,0,-32,0,0,32\), and elimination certifies the matching upper bound \(v_{C_4}=512\). Independently sum \(T_a(z)^4\) over the same rows to compute \(\xi_H\).
